newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistan newspapers - April 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistan newspapers - April 8.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Food riots brought Peshawar to a standstill as people looted several general stores and shops, besides blocking the roads.
- The Punjab provincial government is working on a war footing to overcome the continuing flour crisis in the province.

- The Pakistan Flour Mills Association has warned of a serious flour crisis in Karachi in the next few days as the "government godowns have now only 3,000 tonnes of wheat as against a capacity of 150,000 tonnes".
- The prime ministers of Pakistan and India will meet in Maldives in May during the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation summit, Foreign Secretary Shamshad Ahmad said.
- Former prime minister Benazir Bhutto would be leaving for London on Tuesday on a private visit, her first trip abroad since the dismissal off her government, PPP sources said.
- Minister for Finance Sartaj Aziz assured the Senate (upper house) that the government has no plans to further devalue the rupee.
- President Farooq Legahri said he avidly supported the scrapping of the controversial parts of the 8th Amendment in the constitution which gave the president the power to dissolve the assembly.
- Exploration in the Kirthar area of the Sindh province has yielded a new gas field and initial estimates put it at over one trillion cubic feet.
- Cabinet Committee on Privatisation will meet in Islamabad on Tuesday to finalise a policy approach for the restructuring and privatisation of the three nationalised banks.
